sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Page head, fonts and base theme
sections.what: Sets the page title, character set, screen-size setting and the font links. Also defines the dark colour scheme, the header and the container layout.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page should look the same on any screen with one consistent dark theme.
sections.watch_out: The fonts load from an outside service, so the page looks different if that service is blocked or offline.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Hero text, input box and main button
sections.what: Styles the large heading, the subtitle, the text input box and the main button, including its disabled look.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the input the clear first step on the page.
sections.watch_out: The button is styled as disabled, so the page's script must enable it. That script is not in the parts shown.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Cards, profile boxes and hidden class
sections.what: Styles the cards, the profile grid, the profile boxes and their labels. Defines a class that hides any element using it.
sections.why: Likely reason: profile boxes show company details in a tidy grid, and the hidden class lets the script show or hide sections.
sections.watch_out: The hidden rule is marked to always win over other display rules, so an element with it stays hidden even when other styles ask it to show.

sections.name: File setup (part 4)
sections.title: Loading spinner and log styles
sections.what: Sets the look of the small spinning circle shown on the build button while work runs. It also styles the scrolling activity log at the bottom of the page, with colored entries.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the user a visible sign that work is happening and a readable record of each step.
sections.watch_out: The log colors come from the color settings at the top of the file, so renaming those settings changes the whole look.

sections.name: File setup (part 5)
sections.title: Company name input and build button
sections.what: Draws the box where the user types a company name, with example names as a hint, and the build button that starts the lookup. It also holds a hidden results area with a profile card and two empty cards that appear once results arrive.
sections.why: Likely reason: the results stay hidden until a lookup succeeds, so the page starts clean.
sections.watch_out: The button calls the function named startBuild, so that function name must stay the same or the button stops working.

sections.name: File setup (part 6)
sections.title: Starting the lookup and showing the profile
sections.what: When the user clicks build or presses Enter, sends the company name to the server. On success it fills in the profile card with industry, business model, and stage, with Unknown when a value is missing. On failure it writes an error to the log and shows an alert. Either way it restores the button afterward.
sections.why: Likely reason: this is a simple one-step lookup, built before the fuller multi-step version in app_old.html.
sections.watch_out: Profile values from the server are placed on the page as raw HTML, so unexpected text from the server could break the layout.

summary: Sets the look of the model-building web page: a dark theme, layout for the header and input form, and styles for cards and profile boxes. Only three of the six parts are covered in this note set.
purpose: Defines how the model-building page looks in the browser.
why: Likely reason: a dark, technical style with bright accent colours suits a finance tool. Reason not otherwise stated in the code.
how: 1. Loads two fonts from Google. 2. Resets spacing. 3. Defines colour variables. 4. Styles the sticky header, the title, the container, the hero block, the input box and the main button. 5. Styles cards, the profile grid and its labels. 6. Defines a hidden class used to hide elements.
inputs: None in the parts shown. The page's behavior (script) is in parts not shown.
outputs: A styled page layout and colour scheme in the browser.
risks: Fonts load from Google, so the page depends on an outside service and visitors' addresses are sent to Google. The hidden class overrides other display settings. Three of six parts are missing, so the page's behavior is not known.
debug: If the look is wrong, check the colour variables first. If the fonts look plain, check internet access. If an element will not hide or show, check whether the hidden class is applied. Check parts 4 to 6 for the rest of the styles.
